questions.q: What is the sum of all the individual digits of the first 100 natural numbers (1 to 100)?
questions.s:
Core Tool Triggered: JSM (Symmetry Counting)

Dekh bhai... series add nahi karni, smart approach lagao. 0 to 99 ek perfect symmetric block hota hai.

Pen-Free Observation: 00 se 99 tak har digit (0-9) apne place par equally repeat karti hai.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique):
00 se 99 tak har digit exactly 20 baar aati hai (10 baar tens par, 10 baar units par, total 10 sets mein).
Sum of digits = $20 \times (0+1+2+\dots+9) = 20 \times 45 = 900$.
Bacha 100, iske digits ka sum hai 1.
Total ho gaya $900 + 1 = 901$. CGL level logic!

Future Exam Takeaway: Exploit symmetry in counting problems. The block 00-99 is your best friend for digit frequencies.

questions.q: If $n$ is a positive integer, then when $1^{n}+2^{n}+3^{n}+4^{n}$ is divided by $10$, how many possible remainders can there be?
questions.s:
The 'Pen-Free' Observation First:
Dividing by $10$ is just finding the Unit Digit! We only need to check cycles of powers up to $4$.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach):
Put $n=1$: $1+2+3+4 = 10 \implies$ Unit digit $0$.
Put $n=2$: $1+4+9+6 = 20 \implies$ Unit digit $0$.
Put $n=3$: $1+8+7+4 = 20 \implies$ Unit digit $0$.
Put $n=4$: $1+6+1+6 = 14 \implies$ Unit digit $4$.
Possible remainders are only $0$ and $4$. That means exactly $2$ possible remainders.

Method 2 (Concept Builder):
The cyclicity of unit digits for $1, 2, 3, 4$ repeats every $4$th power. So checking $n=1,2,3,4$ covers all infinite possibilities.

Future Exam Takeaway:
Divisibility by $10$ ALWAYS means 'Find the Unit Digit'. Don't waste time thinking about complex polynomial theorems. CGL bas unit digit check karwana chahta hai!

questions.q: Find the least number which is completely divisible by $9, 24$ and $36$?
questions.s:
The 'Pen-Free' Observation First:
'Least number completely divisible' matlab sedha-sedha LCM (Lowest Common Multiple) pucha hai. Language ghumaai hai bas.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach):
Numbers hain $9, 24, 36$.
Notice karo ki $36$ exactly $9$ se divide hota hai. Toh $9$ ko picture se hi hata do.
Ab sirf $24$ aur $36$ ka LCM nikalna hai.
Highest common factor of $24, 36$ is $12$.
LCM = $12 \times (2 \times 3) = 72$. Option dekhte hi mark karo!

Method 2 (Concept Builder):
Jab given set of numbers me koi chota number kisi bade number ka factor ho, toh chote number ka LCM par koi effect nahi padta.

Future Exam Takeaway:
Don't draw lines and solve for LCM blindly. Eliminate factors immediately to shrink your calculation.

questions.q: Three fractions $x, y$ and $z$, are such that $x > y > z$. When the smallest of them is divided by the greatest, the result is $9/16$, which exceeds $y$ by $0.0625$. If $x+y+z = 1 \frac{13}{24}$ then the value of $x+z$ is:
questions.s:
Core Tool Triggered: Unitary Scaling (Fraction Decoding)

Dekh bhai aise karna hai... Language me extra details ko ignore karke direct fraction attack karo.

Pen-Free Observation: Main loop hai $0.0625$ ko decode karna, jo directly $\frac{1}{16}$ ka fraction value hota hai.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach): Question kehta hai ki $\frac{z}{x} = \frac{9}{16}$ aur ye $y$ se $\frac{1}{16}$ zyada hai.
Yani $y = \frac{9}{16} - \frac{1}{16} = \frac{8}{16} = \frac{1}{2}$.
Sum diya hai: $x + y + z = \frac{37}{24}$.
Hamein chahiye $x + z$. Toh seedha sum me se $y$ uda de!
$x + z = \frac{37}{24} - \frac{1}{2} = \frac{37}{24} - \frac{12}{24} = \frac{25}{24}$.

Method 2 (Concept Builder): Fractions aur unki decimal values ($0.0625 = 1/16$) rata hona chahiye.

Future Exam Takeaway: Language chahe kitni ghumaye, fraction conversions dimag me ready rakho.

questions.q: Find the total number of distinct prime factors of the product: $10! \times 11! \times 12! \times \dots \times 20!$
questions.s:
Core Tool Triggered: Unitary Scaling

Dekh bhai, seedha logic! Pura calculate karna hi nahi hai, numbers ka behavior samajh.

Pen-Free Observation: Factorials multiplication mein naye primes generate nahi hote, jo sabse bada boundary number hota hai, highest prime bas uske andar ka hota hai.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique):
Yahan limit 20! hai, matlab jo prime numbers 20 tak hain, sirf wahi is pure product mein honge.
Primes $\le 20$ nikal: 2, 3, 5, 7, 11, 13, 17, 19.
Count karega toh exact 8 aayenge. Aise questions ko second mein uda.

Future Exam Takeaway: Factorial products don't introduce new primes, they just increase the power of existing ones up to the highest boundary.

questions.q: Find the unit digit of $348^{114^{115^{116}}}$.
questions.s:
Answer is 6.

Pen-Free Observation: Dekh bhai, power tower dekh kar ghabrana nahi hai. Base ka unit digit 8 hai. Humein bas check karna hai ki power 4 ka multiple hai ya nahi.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique):
Power $= 114^{115^{116}}$. Yeh clearly ek even number hai kyunki base 114 even hai.
Kya yeh 4 se divide hota hai? $114 = 4k + 2$.
So, $(4k+2)^{\text{power > 1}}$. Koi bhi number jo 2 (mod 4) ho, uski power 2 ya usse badi karne par wo hamesha 4 ka multiple ban jata hai (e.g., $2^2=4, 6^2=36$).
Matlab, poori power perfectly divisible by 4 hai.
Toh $8^4$ projection use kar. $8 \times 8 \times 8 \times 8 \implies 4 \times 4 = 16$. Terminal digit is strictly 6.

questions.q: A number consists of two digits and the digit in the ten's place exceeds that in the unit's place by $5$. If $5$ times the sum of the digits is subtracted from the number, the digits of the number are reversed. Then the sum of the digits of the number is:
questions.s:
The 'Pen-Free' Observation First:
Basic number system property: $(N - \text{Reverse of } N) = 9(x-y)$. Direct equation put karni hai, no lengthy algebra.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach):
Given: Tens digit exceeds units by $5 \implies x - y = 5$.
Standard Rule: $N - \text{Reverse} = 9(x-y) = 9(5) = 45$.
Question says: $N - 5(x+y) = \text{Reverse} \implies N - \text{Reverse} = 5(x+y)$.
Equating both: $5(x+y) = 45 \implies x+y = 9$.
Bhai sum directly $9$ aa gaya, number was $72$. Options dekhte hi khatam!

Method 2 (Concept Builder):
Agar details verify karni ho: $x-y=5$ aur $x+y=9$. Solve kiya toh $x=7, y=2$. Number $72$ ban gaya. Reverse $27$. $72 - 27 = 45$. Condition satisfied.

Future Exam Takeaway:
Difference between a $2$-digit number and its reverse is ALWAYS $9(x-y)$. Sum is ALWAYS $11(x+y)$. Isko muh-zubaani yaad rakho.

questions.q: Six bells commence tolling together at 7:59 am. They toll at intervals of $3, 6, 9, 12$ and $15$ seconds respectively. How many times will they toll together till 8:16 am? (excluding the toll at 7:59 am)
questions.s:
Core Tool Triggered: JSM (LCM Interval Scaling)

Dekh bhai aise karna hai... interval wale question hamesha LCM se chalte hain.

Pen-Free Observation: LCM ka direct execution hai. Values $3, 6, 9, 12, 15$ choti hain, inka LCM mentally $180$ seconds aana chahiye.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach): LCM of $3, 6, 9, 12, 15 = 180$ seconds = $3$ minute.
Time kitna available hai? 7:59 se 8:16 am tak total $17$ minute hain.
Har $3$ minute par toll hoti hai. Toh $17$ minute me kitni baar aayega? $17 \div 3 = 5$ times (ignoring the fraction).
Question ne directly 'excluding start toll' bola hai, toh $+1$ wali tension nahi leni. Answer exact $5$.

Method 2 (Concept Builder): Total Times = $\lfloor \frac{\text{Total Duration}}{\text{LCM}} \rfloor$. Agar initial include karne bole tab $+1$ hota hai.

Future Exam Takeaway: Traffic light aur Toll bell questions me language padh lena ki initial occurrence add karni hai ya minus.

questions.q: Find the number of distinct prime factors of 536.
questions.s:
The 'Pen-Free' Observation First:
Dhyan se padh - \"distinct prime factors\". Matlab base kaun kaun se unique primes hain wo ginna hai, total factor nahi!

Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach):
536 ko jaldi todo:
Last digits 36 hain toh 4 se jayega: $536 = 4 \times 134$
Aur ek 2 nikal lo: $4 \times 2 \times 67$
$536 = 2^3 \times 67^1$.
67 khud ek prime number hai. Toh bases dekho: ek 2 hai, aur ek 67 hai.
Total distinct prime factors siraf 2 huye.

questions.q: The $55x41y$ is a six-digit even number and is completely divisible by $33$, then among the following $(x^2 + y^2)$ is divisible by: ($x$ and $y$ are non-zero)
questions.s:
Core Conceptual Tool: Divisibility & C9.

Pen-Free Observation: Even aur divisibility dono variables fasa rhi hai. Piche $y$ constraint sirf even lega $0$ neglect karke (non-zero). Phir substitution linear equations lagani hogi.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique): Last digit even hai, non zero. Substitue $y \in \{2,4,6,8\}$. $11$ ka divisibility format setup karke single bound output pick karo jo $3$ ka rule set follow kare.

Mathematically :-

$$ \text{11 diff: } (5+x+1) - (5+4+y) = x-y-3 = 0 \text{ or } 11 \\ x-y = 3 \implies x = y+3 \\ \text{3 Sum: } 15+x+y = \text{multi 3} \implies x+y = 3k \\ \text{Put } y=6 \implies x=9. \text{ (Sum } x+y=15 \text{ passed rule of 3)} \\ 9^2 + 6^2 = 81 + 36 = 117 = 13 \times 9 $$

Method 2 (Concept Builder): Full scale equation elimination process in variables limits constraints.

Mathematically :-

$$ x - y \equiv 3 \pmod{11} \text{ (Since diff limit checks)} \\ x + y \equiv 0 \pmod 3 \\ \text{Try } y=2 \to x=5 (5+2=7 \text{ not } /3) \\ \text{Try } y=4 \to x=7 (7+4=11 \text{ not } /3) \\ \text{Try } y=6 \to x=9 (15 \pmod 3=0) \\ 81 + 36 = 117 $$

TCS Trap: Students word "Even Number" ignore kar dete hain initial me ya phr non zero nahi padhte aur $y=0$ pe attempt shuru kar dete hain.

Exam Takeaway:

> Overlapping parameters given hon to filter limit (Even / Non Zero) ko core variable base assume kiya karo calculation filter karke.

questions.q: What is the remainder when $1! + 2! + 3! + \dots + 1000!$ is divided by $18$?
questions.s:
Answer is 9.

Pen-Free Observation: Series of factorials mei hamesha ek collapse point dhundho jahan se terms perfectly divisible ho jayein. 18 banane ke liye $9 \times 2$ chahiye.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique):
Notice kar ki $6! = 720$, jo ki 18 se perfectly divide hota hai. Toh $6!$ aur uske aage saare aane wale factorials ($7!, 8!, \dots$) me bhi 18 chupa hoga. Un sabka remainder zero ho gaya.
Game bas pehle 5 terms me bacha: $1! + 2! + 3! + 4! + 5! = 1 + 2 + 6 + 24 + 120 = 153$.
Ab $153$ ko 18 se divide kar de. $18 \times 8 = 144$.
Active remainder strictly collapses to $153 - 144 = 9$.

questions.q: Find the remainder when $55^{55^{55}}$ is divided by $14$.
questions.s:
Answer is 13.

Pen-Free Observation: Jab negative remainder chamak jaye na, toh maths aasan ho jati hai. $14 \times 4 = 56$, toh $55$ base ko mod 14 me $-1$ likh sakte hain.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique):
Base $= 55 \equiv -1 \pmod{14}$.
Power $= 55^{55}$ jo ki clearly ek odd number hai.
So equation ban jayegi: $(-1)^{\text{odd}} = -1$.
Remainder hamesha positive hona chahiye, so structurally $-1 + 14 = 13$ yields the final result.

questions.q: What are the last two digits of the product of the first $20$ odd prime numbers?
questions.s:
Core Tool Triggered: Unitary Scaling (Modular Trap)

Dekh bhai aise karna hai... options ka elimination aur modulo hack lagana padega.

Pen-Free Observation: Number 'odd primes' ka product hai. Yani isme ek baar $5$ aayega. Lekin ye number $25$ se divide nahi hoga kyunki prime set me dusra $5$ nahi hota. Toh last digits hargiz $25$ ya $75$ nahi ho sakte!

Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach): Mod 4 and Mod 5 ka hack laga.
Product $P$ me $5$ nahi hai ($5$ alag rakh). Baaki primes ko Mod $4$ pe dekho.
Primes $\equiv 3 \pmod 4$ ki counting $11$ hogi pehle $20$ me. Unka product $(-1)^{11} \equiv 3 \pmod 4$.
Toh remaining product $P \equiv 3 \pmod 4$.
And $P \pmod 5$ calculate karne par $2$ aayega. CRT se $P = 4m+3 \equiv 2 \pmod 5 \implies m \equiv 1 \pmod 5$.
Toh last digits $5(20m+15)$. For $m=1$, value $= 35$.

Method 2 (Concept Builder): Ye highly logical CDS trap hai. Aapko pata hona chahiye ek single $5$ multiply hone par last 2 digit hamesha odd multiple of $5$ deta hai but not a multiple of $25$.

Future Exam Takeaway: Product of distinct primes kabhi bhi $25$ se divisible nahi hota, isliye wo kabhi $25$ ya $75$ par end nahi hoga.

questions.q: The sum of four consecutive two-digit odd numbers, when divided by 10, yields a perfect square. What is the smallest of these four numbers?
questions.s:
The 'Pen-Free' Observation First:
Sum ko 10 se divide karne pe perfect square ban raha hai, iska matlab sum exactly ek perfect square $\times 10$ hoga (jaise 90, 160, 250). Chote options se check karo.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach):
Dekh bhai, seedha options se khel! Smallest number pucha hai.
Take 27: sum = $27+29+31+33 = 120$. $120/10 = 12$ (Not perfect square).
Take 37: sum = $37+39+41+43 = 160$. $160/10 = 16 = 4^2$ (Perfect square). Yahi tera answer hai, 5 seconds ka kaam!

Method 2 (Concept Builder):
Basic se: Numbers assume kar $x, x+2, x+4, x+6$. Inka sum $4x + 12$. Question keh raha hai $\frac{4x+12}{10} = k^2$. Aise algebra banane me CGL ka cutoff nikal jayega, options is best!

Future Exam Takeaway:
Jaha 'perfect square' ya 'cube' condition ho, reverse option checking is the supreme hack.

questions.q: What is the remainder when the number 58627316892 is divided by 7?
questions.s:
The 'Pen-Free' Observation First:
Bade number ko 7 se bhag karne ka normal tarika time khayega. Seedha 3-3 digits ke blocks (right to left) banake Osculator method/Alternate Sum method lagao.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach):
Number: $058, 627, 316, 892$.
Alternate Add/Subtract karo:
$+ 892 - 316 + 627 - 058$.
Calculate: $(892 + 627) - (316 + 58) = 1519 - 374 = 1145$.
Ab is 1145 ko 7 se bhag de do, easy padega.
$1145 = 7 \times 163 + 4$.
Remainder seedha 4 aagaya.

Future Exam Takeaway:
Ye same 3-digit alternating block rule 11 aur 13 ke liye bhi perfectly kaam karta hai.

questions.q: The simplification of $(1.\bar{3} \times 1.\bar{3} \times 1.\bar{3} - 1) / (1.\bar{3} \times 1.\bar{3} \times 1.\bar{3} + 1)$ is:
questions.s:
Core Tool Triggered: Unitary Scaling

Dekh bhai... Bar decimals ko algebraically handle karna sikho.

Pen-Free Observation: Expression is just $(x^3 - 1) / (x^3 + 1)$. Bar repeat logic laga kar fraction le lo.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique):
$1.\bar{3} = 1 + 3/9 = 4/3$. Direct substitution kar de.
Equation banegi $\frac{(4/3)^3 - 1}{(4/3)^3 + 1}$.
Ise khol: $\frac{64/27 - 1}{64/27 + 1} = \frac{37/27}{91/27}$.
Denominators (27) cancel hue, answer aa gaya $37/91$. Basic identity trap thi bas!

Future Exam Takeaway: Convert repeating decimals to fractions immediately before applying any algebraic identities to avoid calculation nightmares.

questions.q: In how many ways can the number $10800$ be written as a product of two co-prime factors?
questions.s:
Core Tool Triggered: Unitary Scaling (Combinatorics)

Dekh bhai aise karna hai... jab bhi co-prime factors puche, sidha base primes count karo, pure group uthane hote hain.

Pen-Free Observation: $10800$ me prime bases $2, 3$ aur $5$ aayenge. Co-prime factors banane ke liye pure-pure base ki family uthani padegi.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach): Number of ways = $2^{n-1}$, jahan $n$ distinct prime bases ka count hai. $10800 = 2^4 \times 3^3 \times 5^2$. Yahan $n=3$ bases hain ($2,3,5$). Formula me daal: $2^{3-1} = 2^2 = 4$ ways. Seedha hack!

Method 2 (Concept Builder): Co-prime matlab HCF $1$. Yani ek prime factor ya toh poora group A me jayega ya poora group B me. Ye distribution of distinct items jaisa hai.

Future Exam Takeaway: Number system me 'ways to express as co-prime product' pooche toh bas prime bases gino aur $2^{n-1}$ thop do.

questions.q: What is the digit at the 100th place of the number $(225)^{40}$?
questions.s:
Answer is 6.

Pen-Free Observation: 100th place matlab last 3 digits nikalne hain, so we need $(225)^{40} \pmod{1000}$. CGL/CDS ka advance level remainder concept hai.

Method 1 (Concept Builder):
Number $= (15^2)^{40} = 15^{80}$.
Mod 1000 nikalne ke liye CRT lagate hain ($1000 = 125 \times 8$).
Part 1: $15^{80} \pmod{125} \implies (3 \times 5)^{80} \implies$ 5 ki power 80 hai toh obviously 125 se divisible hoga, so remainder is 0.
Part 2: $15^{80} \pmod 8 \implies (-1)^{80} = 1$.
So number $N$ 125 ka aesa multiple hai jo 8 se divide karne par 1 remainder de. Multiples check kar: 125(rem 5), 250(rem 2), 375(rem 7), 500(rem 4), 625(rem 1).
Match mil gaya! Terminal triad (last 3 digits) is 625. Toh 100th place (hundreds digit) naturally 6 hai.

questions.q: The 6-digit number $537xy5$ is divisible by $125$. How many possible values can the digit $x$ take?
questions.s:
The 'Pen-Free' Observation First:
Divisibility by $125$ ($5^3$) means checking ONLY the last $3$ digits. Poora number ignore maaro.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach):
Last $3$ digits hain $xy5$.
$125$ ke $3$-digit multiples ending in $5$ are: $125, 375, 625, 875$.
Yani $x$ ki place pe values ho sakti hain: $1, 3, 6, 8$.
Total possible values for $x$ are exactly $4$.

Method 2 (Concept Builder):
Jaise $8$ ($2^3$) ke liye last $3$ digits dekhte hain, waise hi $125$ ($5^3$) ke liye karte hain. Even endings ($250, 500, 750$) valid nahi the kyunki unit digit fix $5$ hai.

Future Exam Takeaway:
Remember the standard endings for $125$: $125, 250, 375, 500, 625, 750, 875, 000$. Direct filter out karo given conditions se.

questions.q: The sum of three consecutive odd natural numbers is 147. What is the middle number?
questions.s:
The 'Pen-Free' Observation First:
Average concepts in AP (Arithmetic Progression) zindabad! Jab terms Odd ginti mein hon (3, 5, 7 terms), unka Average hamesha bilkul center (middle) wali term hoti hai.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach):
Seedha Average nikal le bhai:
$\frac{\text{Sum}}{\text{Number of terms}} = \frac{147}{3} = 49$.
Yehi tera middle number hai. Equation $(x + x+2 + x+4)$ banane walo ka selection nahi hota time pe.

Future Exam Takeaway:
JSM or AP average rules save you 30 seconds minimum here.

questions.q: What is the sum of the first $39$ odd numbers?
questions.s:
Final Output: $1521$

Core Conceptual Tool: Fixed Identities.

Pen-Free Observation: Dekh bhai, pehle $n$ odd numbers ka sum manga hai, series dekh kar sidha lag raha hai formula trick se udayenge.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique): AP wagera ka lamba formula bhul ja. First $n$ odd terms bola hai toh seedha $n^2$ wali trick lapet aur aage badh.

Mathematically :-

$$ n^2 = 39^2 = 1521 $$

Method 2 (Concept Builder): Agar bhool jaye toh Arithmetic Progression (AP) ka formula use kar, jisme first term $a=1$ and common difference $d=2$ hoga.

Mathematically :-

$$ S_n = \frac{n}{2}(2a + (n-1)d) \\ S_{39} = \frac{39}{2}(2(1) + 38(2)) = 1521 $$

TCS Trap: TCS chahega tu poora AP likh ke time waste kare, usme nahi fasna hai time bacha.

Exam Takeaway:

> First $n$ odd numbers ka sum hamesha $n^2$ hota hai. First $n$ even pucha hota toh $n(n+1)$ hota.

questions.q: Find the number of even factors of $N = 2^{5} \times 3^{4} \times 5^{3}$ which are also perfect squares.
questions.s:
The 'Pen-Free' Observation First: 'Even factor' ka matlab hai ki prime factorization me $2$ zaroor hona chahiye. 'Perfect square' ka matlab hai powers even honi chahiye.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach):
Dekh bhai, combinations banate hain:
$2$ ki powers: Perfect square ke lie $0, 2, 4$ chahiye. Par Even condition ne $2^0$ ko reject kar diya. Toh choice bachi: $2^2, 2^4$ (Total 2 options).
$3$ ki powers: Square ke lie $0, 2, 4$ (Total 3 options).
$5$ ki powers: Square ke lie $0, 2$ (Total 2 options).
Sabko multiply kar do (Fundamental Principle of Counting): $2 \times 3 \times 2 = 12$. Option A is correct.

Method 2 (Concept Builder):
A factor $F$ is a perfect square if its prime decomposition has only even exponents. The 'even' constraint specifically forces the prime $2$'s exponent to be strictly greater than $0$.

Future Exam Takeaway: Combinatorics based factors questions me conditions ko overlapping parts me break karke independent choices multiply karna is the most robust way.

questions.q: How many composite factors does the number $2^3 \times 3^2 \times 5^1$ have?
questions.s:
The 'Pen-Free' Observation First:
Total factors nikal ke Primes aur '$1$' ko hata dena hai.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach):
Formula: Composite = Total Factors - Prime Factors - 1.
Total = $(3+1)(2+1)(1+1) = 4 \times 3 \times 2 = 24$.
Prime bases are $2, 3, 5$ (Total $3$ primes).
Composite = $24 - 3 - 1 = 20$.

Method 2 (Concept Builder):
Every factor is either Prime, Composite, or Neither (which is $1$). Isiliye humesha $1$ subtract karna mat bhulna, ye CDS ka classic trap hai!

Future Exam Takeaway:
Keep this equation tattooed in memory: Total Factors = Prime + Composite + 1.

questions.q: $64329$ is divided by a certain number. While dividing, the numbers, $175, 114, 213$ appear as $3$ successive remainders. The divisor is:
questions.s:
The 'Pen-Free' Observation First: Division algorithms me consecutive intermediate remainders humein Divisor ke direct multiples dedenge via subtraction.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach):
Bhai, Divisor guess karne ke reverse engineering ko samajh:
First step: 3 digits lo $643$. Isme se Divisor $D$ ghata ke $175$ aaya. Yani $D \times x = 643 - 175 = 468$.
Second step: Agla digit utara, number bana $1752$. Isme se ghatake $114$ bacha. $D \times y = 1752 - 114 = 1638$.
Third step: Last digit laaye, bana $1149$. Ghataya toh $213$ remainder. $D \times z = 1149 - 213 = 936$.
Ab aisa $D$ dhoondho jo $468, 1638,$ aur $936$ teeno ka factor ho (yani unka HCF).
HCF trick: $468$ aur $936$ clearly $468$ me related hain ($468 \times 2 = 936$). Ab $468$ aur $1638$ ko dekho, $468$ ka half $234$ kya dono me lag raha hai? $234 \times 7 = 1638$ aur $234 \times 4 = 936$. Yes! Toh Divisor = $234$.

Method 2 (Concept Builder):
Long division steps strictly equate to: $\text{Dividend block} - \text{Divisor Multiple} = \text{Remainder}$. Collecting all difference equations provides numbers that all share the Divisor as a common factor.

Future Exam Takeaway: Jab bhi intermediate remainders diye hon, unhe 'New Formed Dividend' se subtract karke seedha unka HCF nikal lo.

questions.q: Find the remainder when $(-13)^{100}$ is divided by $14$.
questions.s:
The 'Pen-Free' Observation First: Base $(-13)$ aur Divisor $14$ ke beech exactly $1$ ka difference hai. Seedha Fermat/Negative Remainder ka application hai.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach):
Bhai, negative base dekh kar CGL me darna nahi. $(-13)$ ko $14$ se bhag dega toh positive remainder kya aayega? $+1$ (kyunki $-13 + 14 = 1$).
Ya direct deviation lagao: $(-13) \equiv 1 \pmod{14}$.
Ab us remainder par original power rakh do: $1^{100} = 1$. Itna lallu sawal free ke marks deta hai.

Method 2 (Concept Builder):
Polynomial theorem ke hisab se: $\frac{(a-1)^n}{a}$. Agar $n$ even hai toh remainder hamesha $1$ hota hai. Yahan $a=14$ aur base $14-27$ ya $-13$ le sakte hain, practically the distance to nearest multiple is what matters.

Future Exam Takeaway: Negative base hamesha modulus add karke positive remainder me convert karo, mistakes zero ho jayengi.
